Tamales De Dulce

Served at: Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Serves 8-10Prep 45 minCook 1 hour

Tamales de Dulce are sweet corn masa tamales traditionally served during Candlemas, also known as the Feast of the Presentation. This holiday, celebrated on February 2nd, marks the end of the Christmas season in Mexico and is a time when families gather to enjoy these sweet treats, often accompanied by atole or hot chocolate.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups masa harina (corn dough flour)
  • 1 cup sugar
  • 1 cup unsalted butter, softened (226 g)
  • 1 cup milk (240 ml)
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 cup raisins (optional)
  • Food coloring (pink or red, optional)
  • Corn husks, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes

Method

  1. Soak the corn husks in warm water for at least 30 minutes to soften them.
  2. In a large bowl, beat the softened butter with sugar until fluffy.
  3. Add the milk and vanilla extract to the butter mixture and mix well.
  4. In a separate bowl, combine the masa harina, baking powder, and salt.
  5. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until a soft dough forms.
  6. If desired, add a few drops of food coloring and mix until evenly colored.
  7. Fold in the raisins if using.
  8. Drain the corn husks and pat dry.
  9. Spread about 2 tablespoons of masa dough onto the smooth side of each corn husk, spreading it into a rectangle about 4x6 inches.
  10. Fold the sides of the husk over the masa to enclose it, then fold the bottom up to secure the tamale.
  11. Place the tamales upright in a steamer basket with the open end up.
  12. Steam the tamales over boiling water for about 1 hour, or until the masa is firm and pulls away easily from the husks.
  13. Remove the tamales from the steamer and let them cool slightly before serving.

Tips

  • For a traditional touch, use natural food coloring from beet juice or annatto seeds.
  • Serve tamales de dulce with hot chocolate or atole for an authentic Candlemas experience.
  • If you prefer, substitute raisins with chopped dried fruit like apricots or cherries.
